requirements.quote: The memory screen lists active items grouped by layer tabs (Profile, Preferences, Matters, Court notes, Clients, Recognition) with a Memory Card per item showing plain-language statement, scope chip (Only you / Chamber / This matter), source chip and last-used time.
A proposal tray shows pending proposals with evidence; each has Save, Edit and Dismiss, and nothing becomes memory without Save; keyboard shortcuts `s`, `e`, `x` work on the focused proposal.

Edit opens a sheet with the value, scope selector (chamber sharing visible only to the owner) and save; delete uses a confirmation dialog stating that embeddings are removed within 24 hours; pause per item and 'Pause all memory' work.
'Used in' popover lists where an item influenced output (brief, draft, matching) with links, using `memory_usage`.

Monthly review is a stepper through items not confirmed or used in 60 days with Keep, Edit, Delete; completing it records the review date and shows a summary; a reminder card appears on the screen when a month has passed.
Tenure panel shows correction rate and brief-accepted-unedited rate by week as simple accessible charts with a data table alternative; no cross-workspace comparison appears.
A clerk opening `/memory` sees a permission-denied explanation, not an empty list; juniors see only personal-scope items and matter memory for their assigned matters.
The matter workspace Memory tab renders the same cards filtered to that matter and cannot show another matter's items.

States: empty ('Nothing saved yet. As you work, CauseDeck will suggest things to remember and ask first'), skeleton, error with retry, offline (read-only cache; edits disabled with explanation), denied.
No screen element profiles a judge or bench; court notes are labelled 'Your own notes' and the add form shows a note about not recording analysis of individual judges.
Light and dark AA; baselines at 360, 768, 1280; initial JS <= 180 KB gzip; Lighthouse performance and accessibility >= 95.
requirements.evidence: CI Lighthouse, Playwright visual and bundle-budget (apps/web/__tests__/bundle-budget.test.ts) jobs on the ship PR; baselines and Lighthouse never run locally

requirements.quote: Storybook stories exist for every new component with all states (default, empty, loading, error, offline, denied) and interaction tests.
Playwright visual baselines exist for light and dark themes at 360, 768 and 1280 px.

decisions.choice: Store the review date as a workspace-scope M1 memory item under new key M1.last_memory_review instead of a new workspace_settings column
decisions.justification: The issue names `M1.last_memory_review`; M1 allows workspace scope (packages/validators/src/memory.ts:30-36) and a migration (packages/db/src/schema/workspace.ts:22) would also require RLS/index test updates per CLAUDE.md; the key is hidden from lists.
